notes:
Rate of change

  • If $y=f(x)$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ gives the instantaneous rate of change of $y$ w.r.t. $x$. For related quantities (e.g. radius and volume of a sphere), use chain rule: $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{dV}{dr}\cdot\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

Increasing / decreasing functions

  • $f$ is strictly increasing on an interval if $f'(x)>0$ there; strictly decreasing if $f'(x)<0$.
  • To find intervals: find $f'(x)$, solve $f'(x)=0$ for critical points, then test the sign of $f'(x)$ in each sub-interval.

Tangents and normals

LineEquation at $(x_1,y_1)$
Tangent$y-y_1=f'(x_1)(x-x_1)$
Normal$y-y_1=-\dfrac{1}{f'(x_1)}(x-x_1)$
  • Tangent is horizontal where $f'(x_1)=0$; vertical (normal horizontal) where $f'(x_1)$ is undefined/infinite.

Approximations

  • $\Delta y\approx f'(x)\Delta x$; so $f(x+\Delta x)\approx f(x)+f'(x)\Delta x$. Used for approximate values like $\sqrt{26}$, $(3.02)^2$, etc.

Maxima and minima

  • First derivative test: at a critical point $c$ (where $f'(c)=0$), if $f'$ changes $+\to-$, local max; $-\to+$, local min; no sign change, neither.
  • Second derivative test: if $f'(c)=0$ and $f''(c)<0$ then local max; $f''(c)>0$ then local min; $f''(c)=0$ then test fails (use first derivative test).
  • Absolute max/min on $[a,b]$: compare $f$ at critical points and at endpoints $a,b$.
  • Standard optimisation: for fixed perimeter/area/volume constraints, express one variable in terms of the other, differentiate, and set derivative to zero.
WordMeaning
Critical point$f'(x)=0$ or $f'(x)$ undefined
Point of inflection$f''(x)=0$ and sign of $f''$ changes

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 3-4 questions here — one rate-of-change numerical, one increasing/decreasing interval, one tangent/normal equation, and one maxima/minima (often an optimisation word problem like maximum area/volume). Keep the sign chart method for $f'(x)$ ready; it is the fastest way to nail increasing/decreasing and extremum questions.

questions.q: The rate of change of the area of a circle with respect to its radius $r$ when $r=5\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2\Rightarrow \dfrac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r=2\pi(5)=10\pi$.

questions.q: A balloon's volume increases at $72\pi\,\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. The rate of increase of its radius when $r=6\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. $72\pi=4\pi(36)\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dr}{dt}=72\pi/144\pi=0.5$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^2-4x+7$ is strictly increasing on
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x-4>0\Rightarrow x>2$.

The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=x^2$ at the point $(2,4)$ is
questions.explanation: $dy/dx=2x$; at $x=2$, slope $=4$.

questions.q: The equation of the tangent to $y=x^2$ at the point $(1,1)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope at $(1,1)$ is $2(1)=2$. Tangent: $y-1=2(x-1)\Rightarrow y=2x-1$.

questions.q: The point on the curve $y=x^2$ where the tangent is parallel to the x-axis is
questions.explanation: Tangent parallel to x-axis $\Rightarrow dy/dx=0\Rightarrow2x=0\Rightarrow x=0$, giving point $(0,0)$.

Among all rectangles with a given perimeter $P$, the one with maximum area is a
options: rectangle with length thrice the breadth
rectangle with length twice the breadth
questions.explanation: For fixed perimeter, area $A=x(P/2-x)$ is maximised at $x=P/4$, giving equal sides — a square.

questions.q: The equation of the normal to the curve $y=x^2$ at $(1,1)$ is
questions.explanation: Tangent slope at $(1,1)$ is 2, so normal slope $=-1/2$. Normal: $y-1=-\dfrac12(x-1)\Rightarrow2y-2=-x+1\Rightarrow x+2y=3$.

questions.q: A ladder 5 m long is leaning against a wall. The bottom slides away from the wall at $2\,\text{m/s}$. How fast is the top sliding down when the bottom is 3 m from the wall?
questions.explanation: $x^2+y^2=25$. At $x=3$, $y=4$. Differentiating: $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}+2y\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-\dfrac34\times2=-1.5$; speed is $1.5\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.q: The interval in which $f(x)=\log x-x$ (for $x>0$) is increasing is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=1/x-1>0\Rightarrow x<1$. Combined with domain $x>0$, increasing on $(0,1)$.

questions.q: The maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in a circle of radius $r$ is
questions.explanation: The maximum-area rectangle inscribed in a circle is a square with diagonal $2r$, side $r\sqrt2$, area $=2r^2$.

questions.q: At $x=0$, the function $f(x)=x^3$ has
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3x^2\ge0$ always (no sign change), so $x=0$ is neither max nor min; $f''(x)=6x$ changes sign at $0$, so it is a point of inflection.

questions.q: The absolute maximum value of $f(x)=x^2$ on $[-2,3]$ is
questions.explanation: Compare endpoints and critical point $x=0$: $f(-2)=4$, $f(3)=9$, $f(0)=0$. Maximum is $9$ at $x=3$.

questions.q: Two positive numbers whose sum is 16 and whose product is maximum are
questions.explanation: Let numbers be $x,16-x$; product $P=16x-x^2$, $P'=16-2x=0\Rightarrow x=8$. Numbers are 8 and 8.

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate change in the volume of a cube of side $x=10\,\text{cm}$ caused by increasing the side by $0.1\,\text{cm}$ is

The rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its radius $r$ when $r=3\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3\Rightarrow \dfrac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$; at $r=3$: $4\pi(9)=36\pi$.

questions.q: A kite is flying at a constant height of 90 m and moves horizontally away from the flyer at $5\,\text{m/s}$. When the kite is 120 m horizontally away (so the string is 150 m long), the rate at which the string is being let out is
questions.explanation: Let $x$ = horizontal distance, height $=90$ (constant), string $l$: $l^2=x^2+90^2$. Here $x=120,\ l=150$ (since $90^2+120^2=150^2$). Differentiating: $2l\dfrac{dl}{dt}=2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dl}{dt}=\dfrac{x}{l}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{120}{150}\times5=4\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=2x^3-9x^2+12x+5$ is strictly increasing on
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=6x^2-18x+12=6(x-1)(x-2)$. This is positive when $x<1$ or $x>2$, so $f$ is strictly increasing on $(-\infty,1)\cup(2,\infty)$.

questions.q: The point on the curve $y=x^2$ where the tangent has slope $6$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x=6\Rightarrow x=3$, and $y=3^2=9$. The point is $(3,9)$.

questions.q: The tangent to the curve $y=x^3$ at $x=1$ is parallel to which line?
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2$; at $x=1$, slope $=3$. The line $3x-y=0$ i.e. $y=3x$ has slope $3$, matching.

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate value of $(8.01)^{1/3}$ is
For $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+15$, the point of inflection is at
questions.explanation: $f''(x)=6x-12$. Setting $f''(x)=0$ gives $x=2$, and $f''$ changes sign there, so it is a point of inflection.

questions.q: A cylindrical tank's volume is increasing at $50\,\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$ while its radius stays fixed at $r=5\,\text{cm}$. The rate at which the height is increasing is
questions.explanation: $V=\pi r^2h\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\pi r^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}$ (r fixed). $50=\pi(25)\dfrac{dh}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{50}{25\pi}=\dfrac{2}{\pi}$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x+\dfrac{1}{x}$ (for $x>0$) has a local minimum at
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow x^2=1\Rightarrow x=1$ (taking $x>0$). Since $f''(x)=\dfrac{2}{x^3}>0$ at $x=1$, it is a local minimum.

questions.q: Among all numbers whose sum is 24, the pair whose product is maximum is
questions.explanation: For fixed sum $S$, product $x(S-x)$ is maximised when $x=S/2$, i.e. the two numbers are equal: $12$ and $12$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin x+\cos x$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, whose maximum value is $\sqrt2$.

questions.q: If the side of a square is increasing at $3\,\text{cm/s}$, the rate at which its area is increasing when the side is $10\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $A=s^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dt}=2s\dfrac{ds}{dt}=2(10)(3)=60\,\text{cm}^2/\text{s}$.

questions.q: The absolute minimum value of $f(x)=x^2-2x+3$ on $[0,3]$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x-2=0\Rightarrow x=1$ (in $[0,3]$), $f(1)=1-2+3=2$. Compare with endpoints: $f(0)=3$, $f(3)=9-6+3=6$. The minimum among these is $2$.

questions.q: At a critical point $x=c$ of a twice-differentiable function $f$ (where $f'(c)=0$), if $f''(c)>0$, then $x=c$ is
questions.explanation: By the second derivative test, if $f'(c)=0$ and $f''(c)>0$, then $f$ has a local minimum at $x=c$.

questions.q: The maximum volume of a cone that can be inscribed in a sphere of radius $R$ is achieved when the height of the cone $h$ equals
questions.explanation: For the classic optimisation problem, maximising $V=\dfrac13\pi(2Rh-h^2)h$ with respect to $h$ gives $\dfrac{dV}{dh}=\dfrac13\pi(4Rh-3h^2)=0\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{4R}{3}$ (rejecting $h=0$).

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}$ on $(0,\infty)$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=-\dfrac{1}{x^2}<0$ for all $x>0$, so $f$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$.

questions.q: Using the second derivative test, the nature of the critical point $x=0$ for $f(x)=x^4$ is
options: the second derivative test is inconclusive, but $x=0$ is a local minimum
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=4x^3=0\Rightarrow x=0$; $f''(x)=12x^2$, and $f''(0)=0$, so the second derivative test is inconclusive. But checking directly, $f(x)=x^4\ge0=f(0)$ for all $x$, so $x=0$ is in fact a local (and global) minimum.

questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the curve $y=x^2-2x+3$ at the point where it crosses the y-axis is
questions.explanation: At $x=0$, $y=3$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x-2$, at $x=0$: slope $=-2$. Tangent: $y-3=-2(x-0)\Rightarrow y=-2x+3$.

questions.q: A wire of length 28 m is cut into two pieces; one is bent into a square and the other into a circle. For the combined area of the square and circle to be minimum, the length of wire used for the square is
questions.explanation: Let $x$ = wire for the square (side $x/4$, area $x^2/16$); remaining $(28-x)$ forms the circle ($r=(28-x)/(2\pi)$, area $(28-x)^2/(4\pi)$). Minimising $A(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{(28-x)^2}{4\pi}$: $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{8}-\dfrac{28-x}{2\pi}=0\Rightarrow 2\pi x=8(28-x)\Rightarrow x(2\pi+8)=224\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{224}{2\pi+8}=\dfrac{112}{\pi+4}$.

questions.q: If the radius of a circle is increasing at $0.7\,\text{cm/s}$, the rate of increase of its circumference is
questions.explanation: $C=2\pi r\Rightarrow\dfrac{dC}{dt}=2\pi\dfrac{dr}{dt}=2\pi(0.7)=1.4\pi\,\text{cm/s}$.
